message.content:
Below is a quick‑look table of the **Canadian federal holidays** that create “long weekends” (i.e., a holiday that falls on a weekday adjacent to a weekend) in 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend itself, it does **not** create an extra day off.)

| Holiday | 2023 Date | Creates a long weekend? | Long‑weekend span |
|---------|-----------|------------------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | ❌ | – |
| Family Day (Ontario, Manitoba, etc.) | Monday Feb 20 | ✅ | **Feb 18–20** (Sat‑Mon‑Sun) |
| Good Friday | Friday Apr 7 | ✅ | **Apr 7–9** (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) |
| Victoria Day | Monday May 22 | ✅ | **May 20–22** (Sat‑Mon‑Sun) |
| Canada Day | Saturday Jul 1 | ❌ | – |
| Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | ✅ | **Sep 2–4** (Sat‑Mon‑Sun) |
| Thanksgiving | Monday Oct 9 | ✅ | **Oct 7–9** (Sat‑Mon‑Sun) |
| Remembrance Day | Wednesday Nov 11 | ❌ | – |
| Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | ✅ | **Dec 23–25** (Sat‑Mon‑Sun) |
| Boxing Day | Tuesday Dec 26 | ❌ | – |

> **Key take‑away:**  
> • **Feb 18–20** (Family Day)  
> • **Apr 7–9** (Good Friday)  
> • **May 20–22** (Victoria Day)  
> • **Sep 2–4** (Labour Day)  
> • **Oct 7–9** (Thanksgiving)  
> • **Dec 23–25** (Christmas)

These are the only federal holidays that give you a three‑day break in 2023. If you’re looking at provincial holidays (e.g., St. Patricks’ Day in some provinces, or other regional observances), you’ll need to check each province’s calendar separately.
